name: Georgia
summary: Very strict, toughened in 2025. Using cannabis in private isn't punished and ≤5 g is an administrative offence, but most other drugs have no or tiny 'small amount' limits, so possession is usually a crime.
poisonControlNote: Unverified: WHO's 2023 directory lists the Toxicology National Information-Advisory Center, Tbilisi, as +995 99 53 33 20 (old format). Call 112 for poisoning.
callingForHelp: No Good Samaritan protection. Since 2025 police can order a drug test on suspicion (not for cannabis) and refusal is an offence; a positive test can bring licence and job bans.

lsd.note: 'Small amount' is only ≤0.00002 g (20 µg), less than a typical tab; anything more is a crime. Smaller: admin fine/detention.

mushrooms.note: All fungi of the Strophariaceae family are controlled and psilocybin has no 'small amount', so any quantity is a crime.

dmt.note: 'Small amount' is ≤0.005 g, below a dose; more is a crime. Ayahuasca contains DMT.

mescaline.note: Peyote (Lophophora) and San Pedro (Echinopsis) cacti are controlled; mescaline has no 'small amount', so any quantity is a crime.

dox.note: DOM and DOB are listed with no 'small amount', so any quantity is a crime.

nbomes.note: NBOMes are listed with no thresholds, so any amount triggers criminal liability.

2c-x.note: 2C-B is listed with no 'small amount', so any quantity is a crime.

2c-t-x.note: 2C-T compounds were not found by name in the national lists; they may be treated as analogues or new psychoactive substances.

5-meo-xxt.note: 5-MeO tryptamines were not found by name in the national lists; they may be treated as analogues or new psychoactive substances.

cannabis.note: Private use by over-21s isn't punished (2018 ruling). ≤5 g dried/10 g fresh: admin offence, repeat = crime; 5–70 g: up to 6 yrs (2025).

ketamine.note: Controlled psychotropic (List III). ≤0.1 g: administrative offence (first time); more is a crime.

mxe.note: Methoxetamine is listed with no thresholds, so any amount triggers criminal liability.

dxm.note: Dextromethorphan is explicitly excluded from the narcotics list, so it is not controlled; medicines rules apply.

nitrous.note: Nitrous oxide is not on the controlled-substance lists.

amphetamines.note: 'Small amount' for amphetamine or methamphetamine is ≤0.005 g, below a dose; more is a crime. Methylphenidate: no small amount.

mdma.note: MDMA has no 'small amount', so possessing any quantity is a crime.

cocaine.note: 'Small amount' is ≤0.06 g; anything more is a crime. Small amounts: fine 500–2,000 GEL or up to 60 days' detention.

alcohol.note: Sale of alcohol to under-18s is prohibited.

ghb/gbl.note: GHB 'small amount' is ≤1 g (below a typical dose); more is a crime. GBL and 1,4-BD were not found on the lists.

opioids.note: Heroin 'small amount' ≤0.005 g; oxycodone has none, so any amount is a crime. Prescription opioids need a prescription.

tramadol.note: Controlled (List II), prescription-only. ≤1 g: administrative offence (first time); more is a crime.

benzodiazepines.note: Controlled psychotropics (List III), prescription-only; using medicines without a prescription is an administrative offence.

maois.note: MAOI antidepressants are prescription-only; harmala alkaloids were not found on the lists; ayahuasca contains DMT (controlled).
